provenance.instrument: City of Erie Zoning Ordinance, Codified Ordinances Part 13, Article 1303 (Ord. No. 80-2005 as amended). ADU added by Ord. 52-2024 (passed 9-18-2024): definition in § 601 and permitted use lists in § 204
provenance.status_detail: ADU definition and permitted-use listings carry Ord. 52-2024, passed 9-18-2024. eCode360 lists one uncodified zoning law, Ord. No. 45-2026 (8-19-2026). Its PDF was read: it designates the Forman Block at 1013-1015 State Street as historic. It does not touch ADUs.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 header: Includes legislation through 10-01-2025. New Laws for Art 1303: Ord. No. 45-2026 only.
checks: The code lists ADU as a permitted use but has no ADU standards section. No size cap, owner rule, number cap or parking rule written for ADUs

A detached ADU is read as a detached accessory building under 205.9: side or rear yard, 6 ft from any dwelling or alley, 3 ft from side and rear lines, 720 sq ft, 15 ft. The code does not say so for ADUs. Confirm with the Zoning Officer
Lot area is set per family (R-1 and R-1A 6,000 sq ft, R-2 2,000 sq ft). Whether an ADU counts as a second family for lot area is not stated. Ask the Zoning Officer
204 says only one principal use per lot in any R district, and listed uses are principal uses unless clearly noted. ADU is listed without a note. How the two rules fit is not stated
Parking: dwellings need 1 per family living unit (302). Half of that in RLB, C-1, C-4. None in C-3. Reading this as 1 space for an ADU is our inference
Short-term rental is a separate permitted use in R districts and needs a license. R-1 and R-1A add parking, screening and one-family occupancy rules (305.49)
An attached ADU (addition or above an attached garage) is part of the principal structure and must meet principal yards: R-1 front 30, rear 30, side 5 least and 15 total (205.8, 205 table)
Detached ADU size: a detached accessory building in an R district may be no larger than 720 sq ft (205.9)

Rental licensing: Ord. No. 40-2026 (7-1-2026) amends Article 330, Landlord and Rental, with new registration and inspection rules. An ADU rented to a tenant falls under it. Not zoning, not codified yet
A dwelling unit holds one family. Family: relatives with up to two boarders, or not more than four unrelated persons (601)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Bureau of Planning and Zoning, City of Erie (page in source_urls). Pending changes: none found that affect ADUs. Census GEOID is the 2020 county subdivision code from TIGERweb.

status.note: Accessory dwelling unit (ADU) is listed under Permitted uses in R-1, R-1A, R-2, R-3, RLB, C-1, C-4, M-1 and W-R. Secondary because 204 also allows only one principal use per lot in R districts.

term.note: A single dwelling unit with provisions for sleeping, cooking, and sanitation whose use is secondary to that of the principal dwelling.

path.note: Listed as a permitted use. Read as an accessory use, since 204 allows one principal use per lot in R districts. A zoning certificate from the Zoning Officer is needed (402).

fallback_path.note: Not stated for ADUs. A lot that fails a standard would need a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

zoning_districts.note: Not listed in C-2, C-3, M-2, W-C, W-C2, W-C3, W-M or IP.

building_types.note: No building type limit in the text. The definition ties the ADU to a principal dwelling or building.

min_lot_sqft.note: No ADU lot size. Lot area is per family. Whether an ADU adds a family for this test is not stated.

value.condition: Lot area is set per family (R-1 and R-1A 6,000 sq ft, R-2 2,000 sq ft). If the ADU counts as a second family, R-1 and R-1A need 12,000 sq ft and R-2 4,000. Not stated. Ask the Zoning Officer.
Only one principal use per lot in any R district. The ADU is read as an accessory use.
An attached ADU must meet the principal front, side and rear yards.
A detached accessory building in an R district: side or rear yard only, 6 ft from any dwelling or alley, 3 ft from side and rear lines, no larger than 720 sq ft, 15 ft high.

gates.note: Open questions and conditions. None decides on its own.

existing_structure_only.note: A detached ADU ... can be built as a stand-alone unit or added to an existing structure such as a detached garage.

historic_bypass.note: No ADU rule tied to historic status.

types_allowed.note: Interior ADU (attic or basement), attached ADU (addition or above an attached garage), detached ADU (stand-alone or added to an existing structure such as a detached garage).

max_sqft.note: No ADU size cap. A detached accessory building in an R district is capped at 720 square feet (205.9). See envelope.

max_share_of_house.note: No share-of-house limit in the text.

min_sqft.note: The 205 intro mentions minimum floor area per dwelling, but no such row was found in the tables read.

max_sqft_accessory_building.note: 'Detached accessory buildings shall be no larger than 720 square feet in size'. R districts. The code does not name the ADU, so applying it to a detached ADU is a reading.

max_height_ft.note: Detached accessory buildings shall be no larger than 720 square feet in size or 15 feet in height. Applies in R districts. ADU use not named.

accessory_structure_max_sqft.note: no larger than 720 square feet in size. R districts only.

setback_front_ft.note: Detached accessory buildings shall be located in the side or rear yard of the principal building.

setback_side_ft.note: at least three feet from any side and/or rear property line. R districts.

setback_rear_ft.note: at least three feet from any side and/or rear property line. R districts.

setback_rear_alley_ft.note: at least six feet from any dwelling or alley.

separation_ft.note: at least six feet from any dwelling. Closer than six feet counts as attached and must meet principal setbacks.

internal_uses_district_height.note: An interior or attached ADU is part of the principal structure, so the district height applies (R-1 and R-1A 35 ft, R-2 45 ft). Attached additions also meet principal yards (205.8).

max_impervious.note: No impervious limit in the 205 tables.

owner_occupancy.note: No owner occupancy rule found in the zoning text.

family_only.note: No family tie required. Each dwelling unit holds one family as defined.

short_term_rental_banned.note: Short-term rental is a separate permitted use in R-1 and needs a license (305.49). Extra rules in R-1 and R-1A. No ADU-specific ban found.

spaces_required.note: Dwellings: 1 per family living unit. Half in RLB, C-1, C-4. None in C-3. ADU not named, so this is a reading.

min_lot_sqft.note: Minimum lot area per family (square feet). Principal yards: front 30 ft, rear 30 ft, sides 15 total, 5 least ft. A detached accessory building uses 205.9 instead (3 ft side and rear).
